root_idea.summary: A lexically diverse root associated especially with singularity or oddness, succession at intervals, loss or blood-revenge, tension, and several concrete objects.
root_idea.development: The evidence does not support one uniform root analogy. The singular/odd sense extends to making things occur singly or successively with intervals, while separate lexical branches concern deprivation and retaliation, bracing or tension, habitual course, and concrete anatomical or material objects.

Displayed as the Quranic adverbial noun تَتْرَى.

senses.definition: To deprive someone of the recompense or due of their deeds; to cause them loss in it.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction with أَعْمَال, the object is the recompense or due associated with one's deeds.

senses.definition: One after another; successively, with an interval or interruption between successive arrivals.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of messengers or other things arriving successively. The interval may be understood as short, interrupted, or extended according to context and lexical interpretation.

senses.definition: The odd or singular one; the unpaired number or entity.
senses.usage_conditions: In وَالشَّفْعِ وَالْوَتْرِ, it is the unpaired counterpart to شَفْع. Traditional interpretations of the Quranic expression include the singular or unequalled One, God, as well as particular individual figures or sacred days.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a number or group single or odd; to render an even number odd; also, to perform an odd-numbered witr prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of numbers and of صلاة الوتر, including prayer performed as paired units followed by a single unit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deprive someone of a relative, property, right, or other due; especially to kill or take away a relative or dependent without allowing retaliation, or to inflict loss in property or right.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence includes literal loss through killing or taking away and extended uses for loss or detriment in property and rights.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Blood-revenge or retaliation for homicide; the seeking or claim of such retaliation; as a verb, to execute blood-revenge, rightfully or wrongfully.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The nouns may also denote wrongful conduct or a crime in the pursuit of retaliation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To overtake someone with a displeasing, harmful, or evil action.
To frighten or terrify someone.
To string, fasten, or brace a bow; to attach its string.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction concerns fitting or tightening the string on a bow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make reports, writings, supplies, or observances follow one another at intervals; to alternate them rather than make them continuous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence includes successive transmissions, supplies arriving repeatedly, and fasting on alternating days.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enable someone to attain or obtain blood-revenge.
To become tense or contracted like a braced bowstring; to be taut or contracted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a sinew, nerve, or vein, and to a horse whose veins are contracted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To occur consecutively or one after another, with intervals or separation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of camels, birds, horses, writings, and other things arriving separately in succession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Singly, separately, or one by one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adverbial use derived from the sense of being single or unpaired.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The witr prayer, especially a single or odd-numbered set of prayer units.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The described practice may consist of paired units followed by a final single unit, or of a single unit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The string of a bow; by extension, a chord of a lute or similar instrument.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Plural forms include أَوْتَار and وِتَار.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The partition, junction, or edge between the nostrils; a corresponding part at the front of a horse's nose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The descriptions vary between the septum, subseptum, junction, and edge of the nostril.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sinew or tendon of the back.
A way, course, mode, or manner of acting; a habitual disposition or consistent practice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for continuing in one established way or disposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road or track that keeps close to a mountain and follows a regular course.
Remissness, languor, or faultiness in an affair or work.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a task, activity, journey, or pace in which there is or is not slackness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Delay.
Confinement, restriction, or restraint.
A ring of sinew or cord used as a target for learning to pierce or cast a spear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ring may be made of bowstring or another string or thread.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rose or rose blossom, reported as white, red, or simply a rose-flower.
A small, round star, blaze, or white mark on a horse's forehead or face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A longer mark is distinguished by another term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One whose relative or dependent has been slain and who has not obtained retaliation; one who seeks blood-revenge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term emphasizes the resulting state of bereavement, separation, and unavenged blood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Consecutive or successive at short intervals; of reports, transmitted successively from one person to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is distinguished from uninterrupted or immediately continuous succession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The vein or frenum on the inner side of the glans of the penis.

cautions: For تَتْرَى, the evidence differs on whether the intervals are brief, interrupted, or extended; the stable lexical core is successive arrival.
The Quranic وَتْر in 89:3 has several transmitted interpretations beyond the basic lexical sense of the odd or singular one.
Lane's printed Quran references use legacy citation conventions; the modern verse and word locations in the examples are taken from the supplied QAC data.
